analysis:
Reviewed the supplied base text of docs/provider/cli-reference.md (lines 1-818) and the partial patch excerpt. This is a documentation-only change. It touches Autopilot wording: waiting_inventory now says an ID is 'outside the Autopilot set' instead of 'outside cached Autopilot consent', and a verified prefetch or `darkbloom autopilot models` adds it to the set. It also adds `status` output fields (`Also downloaded`, `Downloads`, `downloads`/`download_usage` JSON) and new Autopilot download limits and disk usage text. No code, protocol, key custody, attestation, logout/revocation, cache-crypto or authorization behavior changes in the supplied evidence.

The security-relevant question is whether the new wording implies that Autopilot can automatically add and download models without operator consent. The base text says verification adds no downloads and that the normal selector downloads only models the operator chooses. The patch excerpt is truncated, and the head text is not supplied, so lines 786-787 and 821-825 on the head side were not seen. The implementation of 'verified prefetch' adding models to the Autopilot set, and the Autopilot download controls, are outside the supplied evidence. I cannot confirm that the set expansion still requires integrity verification (manifest or registry hash, T-012/T-027) or that downloads respect operator limits. Integration should check the head-side docs and Autopilot sources for any weakening of consent, hash verification, or the 'cannot be loaded by ordinary routing' guarantee. No threat-model entry is invalidated by the visible content. The T-041 cache text and the logout text (A-008, T-053) are unchanged context.
